doc.title: Delfeayo Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opening chat and reaction to the Jazz Masters award
summary: Brown and Marsalis reconnect after the Lincoln Center NEA Jazz Masters ceremony; Marsalis calls it inspiring and humbling and says his life is dedicated to jazz.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: Funding for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Program NEA Jazz Master interview was provided by the National Endowment for the Arts.
Interviewer: Anthony Brown with recording engineer Ken Kimery Description: Transcript, 38 pp.
Ferdinand Delfeayo Marsalis. Good to see you again.
It’s been, when? – since you were working with Max and the So What brass quintet. So that was about 2000, 2001?
So that was the last time we spent some time together.
Had a couple of chalupas since then.

I knew you had to get that in there. First of all, we reconnected just the other night over – Tuesday night over at the Jazz Masters Award at Lincoln Center. So, what did you think? Did you have a good time?
I did, to be around the true legends and masters of jazz. It was inspiring and humbling, and they’re cool too.
What do you think about receiving the award?

I still feel I might be on the young side for that, but I think that my life has been, so far, dedicated to jazz and furthering the cause of jazz, and it’s something that I hope to keep doing to my last days.
